subject: MAP: Dedicated + Private capacity — GPU mix, regions, throughput targets
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Wong <jessica.wong@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Dedicated + Private capacity — GPU mix, regions, throughput targets

Hi Jessica / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the MAP sync earlier. Per our run-through, I attached an updated MAP spreadsheet (MAP_v3_ACME_sizing.xlsx) with the current assumptions and a proposed commit plan. Key asks for this week:

- Confirm target throughput goals per region (tokens/sec and concurrent sessions).
- Approve GPU family preference (A800 vs H100) for dedicated pools and whether we should plan a private on-prem pilot in EU.
- Identify the internal lead for procurement sign-off and timing for SOC2 evidence.

High-level summary (proposal):
- US (primary): 16 x A800 (dedicated), target 1200 reqs/min, 50 concurrent sessions peak.
- EU (private candidate): 8 x H100 (private VPC), target 400 reqs/min, 15 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput tuning: prefer batching with 40-60 token windows; we expect 10-15% latency variance depending on sequence length.

Next steps: please review the spreadsheet and reply with any adjustments by EOD Thursday so we can lock the sizing for the procurement worksheet. We'll hold a short checkpoint on Friday to finalize commit numbers.

Attachments: MAP_v3_ACME_sizing.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
Also attaching network-topology-diagram.pdf referenced in the MAP (diagram shows private VPC peering options).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jessica Wong <jessica.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Dedicated + Private capacity — GPU mix, regions, throughput targets

Thanks Vanessa — received and reviewed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- US numbers look reasonable. Can you validate the 50 concurrent sessions peak against a 95th percentile latency SLO of 250ms? We need latency posture details for our performance team.
- For EU, we'd prefer a smaller private footprint initially — can we start with 6 x H100 instead of 8? We expect lower early uptake in EU but want headroom for month 2.
- Procurement: we'll need a short summary of failover/fallback behavior (e.g., how requests route to hosted variants if private capacity is saturated) to include in our contract appendix.

Also copying Procurement for timeline: we need final sizing and budget numbers by Friday COB to start PO paperwork next week.

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Dedicated + Private capacity — GPU mix, regions, throughput targets

Jessica — thanks for the fast review. A few engineering notes from our sizing perspective: 

- 95th pct latency SLO @ 250ms: with 16 x A800 we estimate headroom for 55-60 concurrent sessions for the text-generation profile used in the MAP (conservative sequence length). We'll include a short appendix with measured p95 numbers from a comparable customer.
- EU private: starting at 6 x H100 is fine; propose an automated scale-to-burst option (burst into dedicated hosted pool in eu-west) to handle month-two spikes. That will be in the updated procurement appendix.
- Failover behavior: requests prefer private endpoints; when capacity is saturated we route to regional hosted variants with token-level cost reporting and automatic fallback to a compatible model family. I'll attach a one-page failover summary to the Drive link.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: p95 latency appendix + test data (due Mon 5/17)
- Vivek: procurement appendix text on failover and billing mapping (due Mon 5/17)
- Vanessa: finalize commit numbers with Acme and update MAP spreadsheet (due Fri 5/14 COB)
- Laura: legal to review procurement appendix (in flight)

Subject: Re: MAP: Dedicated + Private capacity — GPU mix, regions, throughput targets — Friday checkpoint notes

Jessica / team — quick wrap from today's checkpoint and agreed commitments: 

Meeting notes: 
- Agreed to commit to 16 x A800 in US (dedicated) with target 1200 reqs/min and p95 latency target ~250ms; engineering will publish measured appendix by Monday.
- EU private will start at 6 x H100 with automated burst into hosted eu-west pool; target 400 reqs/min.
- Failover: private -> regional hosted variant with clear billing mapping; Vivek will draft the procurement appendix.

Action owners & deadlines: 
- Marissa Cole: p95 appendix, test results, and one-page failover summary (Drive) — due Mon 2027-05-17 17:00 PDT.
- Vivek Kulkarni: procurement appendix text and cost mapping for burst behavior — due Mon 2027-05-17 17:00 PDT.
- Vanessa Ortiz: update MAP_v3_ACME_sizing.xlsx with EU change to 6 x H100 and finalize numbers for PO — completed (version v3.1 uploaded).
- Laura Bennett: legal to confirm contract appendix language and confirm SOC2 evidence timeframe — reviewing now.

Next checkpoint: weekly MAP sync — Friday 2027-05-21 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). If Procurement needs earlier PO-ready numbers, flag an ad-hoc on Monday.

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2027-Q3-001) and MAP spreadsheet (https://drive.google.com/open?id=MAP_v3_ACME_sizing).
